{
  "hypothesis": "Predicted that socio-affective functions (empathy) would be intact in old age, extending the socio-emotional selectivity theory.",
  "design": "mixed, between-subject factor age group (younger vs. older adults) and within-subject factor emotionality (neutral vs. negative video clips).",
  "manipulation_or_predictor": "Viewing of neutral versus emotionally negative video clips.",
  "outcome_measure": "Empathic responding, operationalized as the difference in valence ratings after viewing neutral versus emotionally negative videos.",
  "population_and_setting": "Community sample of healthy younger and older adults recruited via a university lab database.",
  "sample_size_total": 107,
  "recruitment_and_incentive": "Recruited via the Lifespan Developmental Neuroscience Lab at TU Dresden; compensated with 8.50 Euro/hour.",
  "analysis_plan": "Repeated measures ANOVA with age group as the between-subject factor and emotionality as the within-subject factor, looking for an interaction effect.",
  "preregistered_or_confirmatory": "not stated",
  "other_methods_notes": "Participants were screened for dementia (MOCA), psychiatric, and neurological conditions. The task used 48 video clips (12 per condition). Response time windows were extended compared to the original task to accommodate older adults."
